hints.title: Greedy Leftmost Correction
hints.text: Whenever the current element is effectively zero after considering prior range inversions, we must perform an inversion starting right at this position, because no future operation can reach back to fix it.

hints.title: Sliding Parity Tracking
hints.text: Instead of modifying k elements each time, keep track of how many active flips currently affect the current position using a running parity or difference marker.

hints.title: Boundary Feasibility Check
hints.text: When an index requires a flip and index + k exceeds the length of the array, completing the transformation is impossible, so return -1. Otherwise mark the flip boundary, toggle parity, and advance.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: length of binary array nums
k: size of bit flip window
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Flipping k consecutive elements directly on each 0 takes O(N * k) time, which degenerates to O(N^2).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Reusing the input array as an in-place marker achieves O(1) auxiliary space while preserving O(N) runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that leftmost-first greedy choices are forced and use difference arrays or sliding flip counts.
complexity.notes: Original array values can be marked with a sentinel value 2 to indicate where flips started.
